svg.title: Organize Discovery Around Buyer Decisions
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-06-buyer-discovery-operating-map; chapter number: 11; title: Organize Discovery Around Buyer Decisions; subtitle: Connect customer language, comparison content, indexing, and attribution to qualified demand.; caption: Federico Jorge on UserActive, Rob Hoffman, Micael Coutinho, and Paul Ogonowski describe complementary discovery functions.; assumptions note: These are operating responsibilities, not a reported staffing chart. Federico Jorge, Rob Hoffman, Micael Coutinho, and Paul Ogonowski do not establish a shared team size or hiring plan.; note: Rob Hoffman reports roughly 10 qualified weekly demos from comparison pages. Paul Ogonowski contrasts 2% of visits attributed to AI in analytics with 23% of new signups reporting AI discovery; the populations differ.; chart type: org_architecture; center: role: Buyer discovery and qualified pipeline; headcount: Not specified; focus: Judge discovery by qualified demand rather than traffic alone, as Rob Hoffman and Loopex Digital emphasize.; spokes: role: Customer-language research; type: Research responsibility; kpi: Buyer questions and wording captured from recorded, transcribed customer conversations, following Federico Jorge on UserActive.; role: Comparison content; type: Publishing responsibility; kpi: Qualified demos associated with comparison pages, tracked through GA4 in Rob Hoffman's account.; role: Search indexing; type: Maintenance responsibility; kpi: Google and Bing indexing checked weekly, with missing pages investigated and improved, following Micael Coutinho.; role: Discovery attribution; type: Measurement responsibility; kpi: New-signup discovery answers and the questions asked of AI assistants, following Paul Ogonowski.
